title: Metric sphere rigidity from the canonical spherical heat kernel by first-eigenspace reconstruction
difficulty_reason: H2 on its distinct spectral/geometric core: the full canonical spherical heat kernel identifies the spectral projection kernels. The author obtains total measure from the zero mode and dimensionn+1 of the first eigenspace from the diagonal projection trace, then reconstructs the cosine-distance bilinear form through evaluation coordinates. A small-time heat-kernel/local-volume dimensional comparison rules out indefinite directions; the chord/length relation and geodesicity give the spherical metric. The final no-hemisphere argument using orthogonality to constants and closed geodesic saturation establishes surjectivity. The evaluation-coordinate framework is reused from the Euclidean unit, but the first-projection trace and global spherical saturation are independent nonroutine H2 work; the research-level Euclidean tangent-cone proof is not inherited as H3.

compared.relation: Actual optim_potentials is a matrix-square-root formula for Gaussian entropic-transport dual variables, not metric reconstruction from a heat semigroup.
Actual identity_for_mu,g gives Gaussian-characteristic-function/sphere-average Fourier identities, not Euclidean or spherical heat-kernel rigidity.
Actual value-error-estimate bounds the discrete partial entropic OT gap byO(log(lambda)/lambda), not a GH rigidity estimate.
Actual th:spherical controls a subgaussian norm for most directions of an isotropic convex body; no heat-kernel/metric-space characterization.

Actual thm1 is four-dimensional Weyl rigidity from pointwise Green-function gradient and curvature pinching on a positive-Ricci Riemannian setting, not exact spherical heat-kernel rigidity on arbitrary metric measure spaces.

Actual boundary-immersion theorem gives a p-form curvature integral inequality and conditional flat-disk rigidity for compact oriented manifolds with boundary, not global heat-semigroup Euclidean-space reconstruction.
Actual intesti is a weighted radial integral bound involving Bakry-Emery Ricci defects and gradient terms; it does not give an almost sharp global heat-kernel estimate from asymptotic volume ratio.
Actual continuum-shuffle compares stopped Jacobi solutions along a measure-preserving flow; different primary from Gaussian kernel/metric rigidity.
Actual weighted volume monotonicity/equality model-ball result under a Ricci lower bound is not the heat-kernel sandwich controlled by asymptotic volume ratio.
Actual intlemma is an elliptic Dirichlet/conformal-field general integral identity, not a spherical heat-kernel characterization.
